# ARB Air Locker Leaks and Cycling

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Apply soapy water to all air locker joints and watch for bubbles forming at the seal rings. [t802]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Apply soapy water to all air locker joints.
2. Watch for bubbles forming at the seals.

_Procedure reported by [t802]._

## Tips & gotchas

- Look specifically at the seal rings where they crimp into tight tolerances. [t802]
- Note that a compressor cycling every 60 seconds indicates an active leak, whereas occasional kicks are normal. [t802]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Assuming constant running is always bad without checking cycle times first. [t802]
- [Partial] Ignoring the front axle seals which are noted as trickier than rear ones. [t802]
